name: differential-analyser-trace
title: Differential Analyser Trace
description: A live/streaming line-chart background modelled on the wheel-and-disc integrator unit of a 1930s Bush-type mechanical differential analyser — a friction wheel rides a steadily spinning disc at a wandering radius, and the adjacent scrolling panel plots the wheel's cumulative rotation as the output curve.
useWhen: an ambient sparkline-style background for a metric card or streaming panel where the mechanic is a physical integrator (a wheel's radius on a spinning disc) rather than a sampled data series; pick sparkline-automaton instead when the backdrop should read an actual KPI series through a cellular-automaton texture, or chart-line-dither when the point is a real scrubbed line/area chart with a readable value at each point — this component has no data prop, no scrub readout and no axis, it only ever plots its own internal pseudo-input signal.
instruction: A card-scale Canvas 2D ambient background modelled on the integrator unit of a Bush-type mechanical differential analyser. The canvas is split into two regions sized from the container's smaller dimension (minDim): a square disc bay minDim wide holding a circle of diameter 0.8*minDim centered in it, and a trace panel filling the remaining width (containerWidth - minDim). The disc is filled with var(--background) so it reads as a porthole through whatever surface it sits on, ringed by a var(--foreground) rim; four spokes fixed to the disc's rotating frame render at 12% var(--foreground) opacity and rotate at the disc's real constant rate of 0.5 rev/s (720deg/s, never stops) — this is the single fast, continuous, real-rate rotation cue, deliberately never discretised so it cannot alias into a strobe. A fixed horizontal carriage arm (15% var(--foreground)) spans the disc's diameter and does not rotate: the wheel — a small circle of radius 0.09x the disc radius, filled at 70% var(--foreground) with a 100% rim and a var(--background) spin-tick line inside it — rides along that arm at x = radiusFraction * discRadius from center. radiusFraction(t) = clamp(0.5 + 0.35*sin(t/4.7) + 0.15*sin(t/1.3), 0.05, 0.95), recomputed every frame from t = performance.now()/1000 (seconds since page navigation origin) — the sum of two incommensurate sine periods means the radius drifts in and out on a roughly 10-15s cycle and the loop never exactly repeats. The wheel's own spin rate follows the real friction-contact physics (equal rim speed at the contact point): wheelRevPerSec = 0.5 * radiusFraction * (discRadius / wheelRadius), visually capped at 3 rev/s so an extreme radius excursion never blurs into a strobe — the disc stays legible because it is the fast element rendered as one smooth continuous rotation, never a discrete flicker. The output shaft's cumulative rotation is integrated on a fixed 20Hz tick independent of both rotation rates (cum += radiusFraction(t) * 0.5 * 0.05 every 50ms, accumulated forever, never reset) and sampled into a ring buffer trimmed to just over 12s of history. Because radiusFraction never goes negative the raw cumulative value only ever climbs, so the trace panel — matching a real strip-chart recorder's AC-coupled zero return — plots each visible sample's deviation from the currently-visible 12s window's own mean, autoscaled every frame to 80% of the panel height: this turns the wheel's wandering integration *rate* (rising while it sits out toward the rim, falling while it drifts toward the hub) into a curve with genuine rising and falling segments rather than a line that only ever climbs off the top. The trace panel has a 1px var(--border) divider from the disc bay (the only use of --border, never a fill or stroke elsewhere), a 4%-opacity var(--foreground) wash so the panel doesn't read as a literal chart 'fill', and the curve itself strokes at 85% var(--foreground) opacity scrolling left at a real 24px/s (matching the 20Hz sample rate: 1.2px per sample). Optional: hovering the trace panel draws a thin luminance-only guideline (30% var(--foreground), no accent tint, no tooltip, no value readout) at the pointer's x — deliberately excluded from ever gaining draggable controls, axis labels or numeric readouts, which would tip this into dashboard territory. All colour is read once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) at mount (--foreground, --background, --border) and re-derived through a MutationObserver on documentElement's class attribute; a ResizeObserver drives canvas sizing (JS-set style width/height, DPR-clamped to 2) and an IntersectionObserver suspends the rAF loop off-screen and resumes it cleanly. prefers-reduced-motion freezes at t = STATIC_PHASE = 3.14 (named 'seconds since a fixed epoch') by synchronously simulating the 12.5s of integrator history that would have preceded it — the same radiusFraction/integrate functions run for negative-relative t, since they are well-defined for any real input — and drawing exactly that one frame with no rAF and no live clock at all; that frame lands with the wheel visibly off-center (well clear of both the rim and the hub) and the trace panel showing both a rising and a falling segment in view, the single most structured frame the loop produces. Root element is aria-hidden with no interactive semantics beyond the optional hover guideline. Zero dependencies, canvas + zero DOM chrome, cleans up rAF/observers on unmount.
